newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-AFRICANS TO CONSIDER CUP CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AFRICANS TO CONSIDER CUP CHANGES.

text.p: African soccer officials are meeting in Cairo this week to approve plans to change the format of the continent's leading club competition, the African Champions Cup.

The executive committee of Confederation of African Football (CAF) is expected on Friday to rubber stamp plans to change the format of the latter stages of the competition to a league competition, bringing it in line with the European Champions League

The reforms will see the African Champions Cup reverting to a league format from the quarter-final stages onwards next year, with the eight teams divided into two groups of four and playing matches both home and away.
The winners of the two groups will qualify for the traditional two-legged final at the end of the year.
"The advantage of this system is that it will avoid the elimination of the competition of good teams, who might have had bad form in a single match," said CAF general secretary Mustapha Fahmy.
"The new system will allow the best two teams to emerge from the groups to contest the final."
The proposed change comes after recommendations in June by an ad-hoc committee specifically created to investigate the possible switch of format.
It is also is reflective of CAF's strengthening relationship with their European counterparts (UEFA).
The two confederations announced several new co-operative projects in July, including a plan for UEFA to donate financial assistance to African countries.
Fahmy said the change would also allow new revenue-generating opportunities for African football through international television rights and sponsorship sales.
These benefits would be passed onto the participating teams, he added, as is the case with the European Champions League.
The earlier two rounds of the competition, which will be played for the 33rd successive year in 1997, will continue on a two-legged knockout basis.
This year's competition has already reached the quarter-final stage with second leg matches to be played this weekend.
